newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar heads lower, could track weak NY.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar heads lower, could track weak NY.

text.p: White sugar futures again edged lower in the early Tuesday trading but activity was quiet before the New York raws open, traders said.
The thin volume was boosted by against actuals manoeuvring in the nearby October contract and some interest was also noted from French producers.
London was likely to maintain its bearish momentum for the time being on account of the hefty spec long position in the New York raw sugar market, they said.
"If it (raws) does wash out, then the whites could move back that way in sympathy as much as anything else," said one trader.
At 1200 GMT October stood down $1.20 at $325.00 and December down 80 cents at $321.00. Volume stayed on the light side at 386 lots, mostly in October.
Fundamentally, the U.S. currency's recent strength is thought to have helped to stifle consumption and acted as a bearish factor.
But traders said this has also been balanced by expectations of lower Thai output next season along with the possible bullish effects of the El Nino weather phenomenon in Asia.
Technical analysts were bullish in the near term and said October looked to be well supported at $325, followed by short-term moving averages at around $320.
"This would lend support to calls for a move higher in price to test $331," said Darren Gurner, technical analyst at Sucden.
Trading on the Paris market was confined to just 172 lots of the two nearby contracts. October was down $1.00 at $324.80 and December down 90 cents at $320.40.
